args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions, with an error rate of about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and work out why v2.3.1 was promoted to production even though the RC failed in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** I picked v2.3.0 because it's the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions are now on v2.3.0. A status check after the rollback shows it healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure and the rollback, and it paged on-call. It also lists next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1, and work out why it reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already been unhealthy in staging.

Approval wasn't needed because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
